title: Teluni Product Documentation
html:
This is the entry point for Teluni-specific product and architecture planning. The product owner's brief of 2026-10-17 is the source of the initial requirements. Engineering documentation is in English; product copy can be localized. Foundation-wide policy remains in the documentation task index.

Reading routes and ownership

Question Canonical document
What is Teluni, who uses it, and what is the commercial hypothesis? Product vision
What name/domains and visual identity are approved? Teluni brand identity
What belongs in the initial release, and how will it be accepted? Release requirements and acceptance
Which product policies were selected, including the PH-09 questionnaire and delegated choices? Release policies
What numeric limits and qualification goals were selected, and which measurements remain pending? Release acceptance targets
Which pilot/trial, pricing, license, quota, support and cancellation policies are approved? Initial commercial policies
What are the accepted architecture directions, proposed module details and unresolved technical choices? Product architecture
How must publication, local playback, and recovery behave? Offline playback and synchronization
How can the residential pilot operate and later move to another host? Deployment and migration planning
What must tenancy, identity, data protection, and localization protect? Security and internationalization
Which human login, recovery, session and permission policies did the owner select? Human identity and access
What evidence supports the accepted identity provider, and what remains unqualified? Identity-provider evaluation
How will tenant-owned data be constrained and scoped in persistence (approved D-01)? Tenant data ownership and access design
How will Keycloak, principals, browser sessions and assurance integrate with the API (approved D-02)? Human identity and session integration design
How will company invitations and durable transactional email work (approved D-13)? Company invitation and durable email delivery design
How will screens be enrolled, authenticated, moved and unlinked (approved D-03 server side)? Device enrollment and lifecycle design
How are media files uploaded, validated, converted, stored and deleted (approved D-05)? Media library design
How are playlists, groups and schedules modeled, validated and evaluated in local time (approved D-06)? Programming design
How are programs published, and how do screens synchronize, verify and report them (approved D-04 server side)? Publication and synchronization design
How does the Android TV player store, verify, schedule and play publications, keep time and update (decided D-07)? Player design
How do catalogs, prices, promotions, layouts and automatic price publication work (decided D-11)? Catalog and composition design
How is the pilot host reached, composed, backed up and recovered, and which email and sign-in providers does it use (decided D-08)? Pilot deployment and recovery design
What may customers upload, how long is each kind of data kept, and how do export, deletion and incidents work (PH-13 decisions)? Data handling policies
What could prevent delivery or safe operation? Risks and dependencies
What is the phase sequence and current execution state? Implementation plan
Which decisions or external prerequisites need a human? Human actions

The owning contributor updates each document with changes to its subject, links related requirements rather than copying them, and regenerates the documentation portal through the contributing workflow. Stable requirement, decision, risk, task, and human-action IDs support traceability; they are documentation references, not implemented registries or API identifiers.

Meaning of status

Product/design status Meaning
Decided A product requirement or inherited accepted direction agreed for planning. It does not mean implemented.
Proposed A candidate solution or acceptance policy requiring evaluation/review. New ADRs start as proposed and become accepted only through explicit review/approval under the ADR process.
Pending An unanswered choice or investigation; no default has been silently selected.
Future Outside the approved initial release and not authorized for immediate implementation.
Implemented Supported by repository code and verification evidence.

Task statuses (pending, in progress, completed, blocked, changed) have the separate meaning defined by the implementation plan. A completed documentation task establishes a specification, not a completed product capability.

Verified baseline

The manifest identifies a derived Teluni project, initialized from Orion commit 53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea. API composition and web composition contain identity and organizations: sign-in, server-managed sessions, optional two-step verification, company creation with creator membership/responsibility, scoped standard-role access, branches and atomic audit. Their tables and references exist; their local tests use disposable Keycloak and PostgreSQL. Membership administration and the broader identity/access scope remain in progress in PJ-03/PJ-24. No player application, media service, deployment manifest or provisioned real environment exists.

This documentation stage does not authorize implementation, deployment, external publication, or acquisition of paid services. The plan identifies the next review and delivery gates.
